method: instrumental response measured on the Xe II 529.222 nm line excited by neutral-beam injection into the vessel filled with Xe to ~0.1 mTorr, B-field off; fitted as a SUM OF GAUSSIANS and CONVOLVED with the plasma Gaussian inside the fitting code (not subtracted in quadrature). Shape depends on fibre position on the entrance slit and slit width (typ. 250-300 um), so it is per-channel and per-wavelength-setting. || dispersion / pixel-to-wavelength from Ne I lines (neon pen lamps in integrating spheres placed in front of the fibres) measured after EVERY discharge; Ne I quartet near 529.05 nm; quoted error <1% on dispersion, ~0.01 px on the pixel->wavelength conversion
valid_from: method in use at least since 1999 (Gohil); re-measured per campaign
reliability: NOT AVAILABLE FROM THIS SITE - method and provenance established from the literature, but no numeric per-chord width is published. The numbers live in the CERFIT calibration on the GA network. DO NOT ESTIMATE.

R_m: 2.18-2.32 (radial coverage; ~8 mm spacing between adjacent chords of same type)
source: C. Chrystal, K.H. Burrell, B.A. Grierson, S.R. Haskey, R.J. Groebner, D.H. Kaplan, A. Briesemeister, 'Improved edge CER in DIII-D', HTPD 2016 / Rev. Sci. Instrum.; OSTI 1287042, Sec. II: 'The dispersion is ~9 pixels/Angstrom'
method: 2/3 m scanning Czerny-Turner, 1400 g/mm grating, SRI Avanti-768 CCD (768x256, 18 um px), 8 view chords per spectrometer on two detectors, two side-by-side slits; 6.2 nm designed wavelength offset between the two slits
reliability: dispersion READ FROM PAPER but quoted as approximate (~9 px/A -> 0.0111 nm/px); per-chord values will differ at the ~1% level. R is the coverage range of the chord set, NOT a per-chord value. sigma/FWHM not published.
